canonical_name: Berkeley Internet Name Domain (BIND) implementation lineage

first_operational.notes: Contemporary Berkeley reports document the implementation by 1984; exact first source release remains to be recovered.

software.version_or_revision: initial Berkeley BIND → CSRG BIND 4.x → later DEC/ISC stewardship; detailed release graph pending

protocols: MX and other DNS resource records

operations.monitoring: Name-server logs/debugging/cache/zone state become critical operations artifacts.
operations.diagnostics: Zone loading, delegation, transfer/refresh and resolver/cache behavior require distinct diagnosis.
operations.remote_management: Zone-transfer/refresh and later control interfaces evolve across releases.
operations.failure_behavior: Misconfigured/stale zones or failed delegation/refresh can break dependent applications while network transport remains healthy.
operations.operator_interface: named configuration, zone files, resolver configuration and debugging utilities.

open_questions: Map 4BSD/4.3BSD integration and BIND 4.x release genealogy.
Preserve early named.boot, zone files and resolver-library source.
Trace CSRG→DEC/Vixie→ISC stewardship with release-level evidence.
notes: BIND is an implementation family, not the DNS protocol itself. Server daemon, resolver library, zone files and institutional custody should eventually be split into finer artifacts.
